overall_summary: The day's tone for Bitcoin is clearly risk-off as hot PCE, strong GDP, and tight labor data lock in higher odds of a December Fed hike. Heavy ETF outflows and fresh geopolitical shocks from the Middle East and tariffs add further pressure on crypto. Limited offsets from the Swiss spot ETF and a Bitcoin reserve bill advancing are not enough to flip the near-term bias.
key_points: Hot PCE and GDP lock in December hike odds
Record Bitcoin ETF outflows hit demand hard
Middle East strikes raise oil and risk-off fears
US tariff proposals add fresh macro headwinds
Swiss ETF and reserve bill offer limited offsets

items.title: Bitcoin ETF outflows hit record $5B+ in November
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs just posted another heavy day of redemptions, pushing November net outflows past five billion dollars and setting a new monthly record. BlackRock's IBIT led the selling again, with seven straight sessions of outflows. Traders should care because these funds remain the biggest source of institutional demand, and sustained redemptions force spot selling that caps any rebound.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure and weaker institutional bid

items.title: Bitcoin reclaims $60k as shorts get squeezed
items.summary: Bitcoin bounced hard from the mid-fifty-sevens back above sixty thousand after hot inflation data and tariff fears triggered the dip. Hundreds of millions in leveraged shorts were liquidated on the way up, adding forced buying. Traders need to watch whether this holds without fresh spot demand, because the move looks more like a squeeze than broad accumulation heading into thin holiday liquidity.

items.title: Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill advances to House floor
items.summary: The House Financial Services Committee formally reported the American Reserve Modernization Act, making a bill to codify the US Strategic Bitcoin Reserve eligible for a full House vote. It would lock government-held bitcoin from sale for at least twenty years. Passage odds look slim with limited time left in the session, but any progress keeps the long-term supply-removal narrative alive for traders.
items.impact: Potential long-term supply lock if enacted

items.title: Galaxy Research withdraws Bitcoin bottom call
items.summary: Galaxy Research pulled its October view that Bitcoin bottomed in June, saying most historical bottom signals remain unmet. The firm now flags a daily close below roughly fifty-eight thousand five hundred as the level that could open another seventeen percent or more downside. Influential research like this can shift positioning and keep risk appetite cautious near current levels.
items.impact: Heightened downside risk if key support fails

items.title: Switzerland launches first spot Bitcoin ETF
items.summary: BIT Asset Management's BBIT fund started trading on the SIX Swiss Exchange as Switzerland's first spot Bitcoin ETF and what the issuer calls Europe's only true spot product. It launched with three hundred fifty bitcoin and a zero-point-one-nine percent fee under FINMA approval. This expands regulated access outside the US at a time when American funds are seeing heavy outflows.

items.title: Hot PCE data lifts December rate-hike odds
items.summary: October core PCE came in at three-point-three percent year over year, above forecasts and the highest in nearly three years, while headline hit three-point-eight percent. Markets now price a December Fed hike as nearly certain. Higher-for-longer rates raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like Bitcoin and helped drive the midweek selloff before the rebound.
items.impact: Tighter liquidity and risk-off pressure ahead

items.title: Hot Core PCE and GDP Surge Lock In December Fed Hike
items.summary: October core PCE rose 0.3 percent month-over-month and 3.3 percent year-over-year, beating the 3.2 percent forecast and hitting a multi-year high. Headline PCE hit 3.8 percent year-over-year. Combined with the Q3 GDP revision, markets now price a 25 basis point December hike at nearly 100 percent, with further tightening odds rising into early 2027. Traders should care because this is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge and the last major print before the December 8-9 FOMC, keeping policy restrictive longer and pressuring risk assets.
items.impact: Higher-for-longer rates headwind for Bitcoin and equities

items.title: Q3 GDP Revised Sharply Higher to 4.3 Percent
items.summary: The second estimate of third-quarter real GDP came in at a 4.3 percent annualized rate, well above the 3.4 percent advance and consensus near 3.5 percent. Upward revisions came from stronger consumer spending at 4.2 percent and business investment, especially AI-related equipment and software. Final sales to private domestic purchasers hit 5.8 percent. This shows resilient domestic demand that reduces recession fears but adds fuel to the Fed's case for more hikes.
items.impact: Reinforces hawkish Fed path and dollar support

items.title: Fed Beige Book Shows Sticky Prices and Wage Uptick
items.summary: The November Beige Book reported slight-to-moderate growth in eight of twelve districts, with four flat. Prices rose moderately and firms expect expenses and prices to keep climbing, while wages accelerated to a moderate pace from modest. Consumer spending was little changed as households stayed price-sensitive, though AI investment remained strong. Released two weeks before the December FOMC, it gives doves little cover and keeps the focus on inflation persistence.
items.impact: Supports additional Fed tightening into year-end

items.title: Jobless Claims Drop to 189k, Labor Market Stays Tight
items.summary: Initial unemployment claims fell 13,000 to 189,000 for the week ended November 21, below the 200,000 consensus, with the four-week average also easing. Continuing claims tumbled to 1.697 million. The report, released a day early ahead of Thanksgiving, points to a stable low-hire low-fire labor market at full employment. Solid jobs data alongside hot inflation further cements expectations the Fed will hike next month.
items.impact: Removes labor-market cover for any Fed pause

items.title: Dollar Pauses Near Highs as Yields Slide on Risk-Off
items.summary: The DXY held around 103.7 to 103.8 into the Thanksgiving holiday after touching multi-month highs earlier in the week. Despite the hot data, 10-year Treasury yields fell as much as 10 basis points toward 4.80 percent on AI valuation fears and safe-haven bond buying. Thin holiday liquidity is expected. Crypto traders watch this closely because a firm dollar and sticky rates typically weigh on Bitcoin, though the yield drop offers some offset.
items.impact: Mixed: hawkish data vs falling yields in thin markets

items.title: Durable Goods Orders Soft Headline but Core Capital Goods Firm
items.summary: October durable goods orders rose just 0.2 percent, missing higher forecasts after a strong September. Ex-transportation orders gained 0.5 percent and core capital goods excluding aircraft jumped 1.2 percent, signaling ongoing business investment strength, particularly machinery. The mixed print fits the broader picture of resilient but uneven growth heading into the holiday-shortened week and December FOMC.
items.impact: Supports growth narrative without major new catalyst

items.title: US Proposes Fresh Tariffs on 14 Major Economies
items.summary: The Trump administration unveiled proposed Section 301 tariffs targeting excess industrial capacity in China, the EU, India, Japan, Vietnam and ten others. Rates range up to 35 percent for some, with China facing an extra 20 percent on top of existing duties, though implementation is delayed for comment and hearings into early 2027 and they largely replace rather than fully stack prior levies. Traders should watch this closely because renewed trade-war risks hit global growth expectations, supply chains and risk appetite across equities and crypto.
items.impact: heightens trade uncertainty and potential inflation pressure on risk assets

items.title: Houthis Claim Strike on Saudi Ras Tanura Refinery
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis said they attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery at Ras Tanura, with satellite imagery showing thick smoke, while Saudi forces reported intercepting drones there. Separately, a drone hit a Riyadh tower housing the Public Investment Fund, injuring 11, and further missiles were intercepted. Oil prices jumped as Brent climbed toward 95 dollars. Crypto traders care because Middle East energy disruptions fuel inflation fears and risk-off flows that typically pressure Bitcoin.
items.impact: oil supply scare lifts energy prices and risk aversion

items.title: Iran Claims Oil Tankers Hit Mines in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers, including a supertanker, exploded and caught fire after striking sea mines north of Oman's Khasab while using unauthorized routes through the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran continues asserting control and warning vessels to coordinate passage amid the wider conflict. This keeps a major chokepoint under threat. For markets it sustains elevated oil prices and geopolitical premium that can weigh on risk assets including crypto.
items.impact: sustains Hormuz shipping risks and oil volatility

items.title: Ukraine Strikes Russian Airbase, Damages Five Jets
items.summary: Ukraine's General Staff reported long-range strikes on the Savasleyka airbase in Nizhny Novgorod damaged three MiG-31 jets used for Kinzhal hypersonic missiles and two Su-34 bombers. The same wave hit Russian oil refineries. Moscow has vowed inevitable retaliation while also striking Ukrainian targets and grain ships. Escalation in the Ukraine war raises broader European security risks that historically drive safe-haven flows and pressure crypto.
items.impact: war escalation risks broader conflict spillover

items.title: Kim Jong Un Calls for Wider Tactical Nuclear Deployment
items.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected nuclear material production sites and the Nuclear Weapons Institute, declaring the nuclear buildup irreversible and urging broader use of tactical nukes across multiple domains and missions. He linked it to the threat from South Korea and warned that denying Pyongyang's nuclear status equates to a declaration of war. This hardens peninsula tensions and adds another layer of global nuclear risk that markets dislike.
items.impact: elevates East Asian nuclear and security premium

items.title: China Demands Japan Stop South China Sea Interference
items.summary: China's defense ministry urged Japan to cease stirring up South China Sea disputes after Tokyo's plans to supply radars and drones to the Philippines. Separately, Japanese and Chinese coast guard vessels clashed near the disputed Senkaku/Diaoyu islands. These flashpoints keep Asia-Pacific military tensions high around critical trade routes. Traders monitor them because any flare-up threatens semiconductor and shipping supply chains vital to global tech and risk markets.
items.impact: ongoing Asia flashpoint risk without immediate break
